Prevention: Use certified crop seed to reduce the chance of contamination.
Seeds are dispersed by water - construct contours and water ways to prevent runoff carrying
Striga seed from infested land to clean fields.
Seeds travel on machinery - clean farm equipment after work in infested areas.
Crop rotation with broadleaved non-hosts and fallows may help to deplete seed bank.
Intercrop with trap crops, like pigeon pea, beans, Mucuna, sorghum, cotton and soyabean to reduce the
Striga seed bank in the soil.
Striga seeds germinate but cannot attach themselves to the roots of crops, so they die.
Improved soil fertility through application of organic, inorganic, green manuring, mulching or agroforestry techniques.
Monitoring: Striga is prevalent in areas with low soil fertility and poor rainfall, such as

Look for a small plant, 10-30 cm tall, rough to touch with bright red or orange-pink flowers growing in close contact with maize.
Direct Control: Light infestations can usually be controlled by hand pulling or weeding before seed set.
Seeds are very long-lived, therefore uproot before seed set
Restrictions: Use of chemical herbicides may lead to the development of herbicide resistance.
